description: "Key takeaways from Module 5."

## Key takeaways

- **Scenes are the unit of experience.** The listener encounters the story one
  scene at a time; the producer renders one scene at a time.

- **Use a narrative arc.** Technical storytelling is not documentation read
  aloud. The eight-beat arc (Introduction, Question, Discovery, Increasing
  complexity, Challenge, Climax, Resolution, Technical takeaway) gives your
  story structure.

- **Every scene needs a learning outcome.** If you cannot answer *what did the
  learner learn from this scene?*, tighten or cut it.

- **Every scene specifies eight fields:** Goal, Technical concept, Location,
  Characters, Action, Sound, Transition, Learning outcome.

- **The climax is the abstraction payoff.** This is where the design decision
  proves its worth — the moment the listener understands *why* the system is
  built this way.

- **Check by reading outcomes alone.** If the learner outcomes cover the
  technical model, the scenes are complete.

## Producing scenes.md

Your output from this module is `scenes.md`. It will be the direct input for
the next module, where you transform it into an audio screenplay.
